questions.question: The essential difference between a wage and a salary is:
options: Wages are more important than salaries
The unit sold — the hour for the wage earner, the year for the salary earner
Salaries are taxed and wages are not
Wages are paid in cash only

questions.question: In the scale R120 000 × R12 000 — R180 000, the middle figure is:
options: The annual increment — the notch added for each completed year of service

questions.question: How many increments does the scale R120 000 × R12 000 — R180 000 contain?
options: Five — the R60 000 distance divided by the R12 000 notch

questions.question: An employee in year two of this scale earns monthly:
options: R11 000 — the R132 000 notch divided by twelve

subtopics.title: Normal Time and the Overtime Multipliers

questions.question: Time and a half on a normal rate of R50 per hour gives an overtime rate of:
Double time normally applies to:
The calculation discipline for overtime is to:
options: Multiply the hours by the normal rate, then adjust
Estimate the total and check it later
Derive the overtime rate first as its own labelled line, then multiply by the hours
Add the multiplier to the hours

questions.question: Gross pay is best defined as:
options: The employer's total cost of employment
What the work earned before any deduction — normal pay plus every overtime category

subtopics.title: A Week at Zanele's Traders — the Wage Run

questions.question: Ndlovu's week (40 normal hours at R50, 3 evening overtime hours) gives a gross of:
Adams's two Sunday hours at a normal rate of R44 earn:
options: R176 — two hours at the double-time rate of R88

questions.question: The week's total wage bill at gross is:
If Ndlovu's three overtime hours had fallen on a public holiday, her gross becomes:
options: R2 300 — the rate line changes to double time at R100

subtopics.title: The Salary Side and Exam Technique

questions.question: The administrator, in her second year on R120 000 × R12 000 — R180 000, earns monthly:
options: R11 000 — one completed year moved her to the R132 000 notch

questions.question: An employee in her third year of service stands on:
options: The notch reached after two increments — completed years count, not the year you are in
The notch reached after three increments

questions.question: The first step in any scale question is to:
options: Add the increment to the ceiling
Write the scale's three parts in words — start, notch, ceiling

questions.question: Comparing the two pay designs:
options: Both change with the hours worked
Both are fixed for the year
The salary responds weekly; the wage grows by annual notch
The wage responds to the week's hours; the salary is a stable twelfth with growth arriving through the annual notch

questions.question: The worker who 'sells hours' is describing:
options: A wage — counted by the clock, landing weekly

questions.question: The 'year deal' fits the office job because:
options: The responsibility is the same in January as in June — a stable slice fits stable work
The law forbids hourly office pay

questions.question: The number both deals produce is:
options: Gross — what the work earned before anything comes off

questions.question: The three rows of the price list for a R50 normal rate are:
options: R50, R75, R100 — plain, time and a half, double

questions.question: Unsocial hours cost the shop extra because:
options: Overtime is taxed at a higher rate
Those hours cost the worker the most to give — weekend, family time, rest

questions.question: The one trap in wage calculations is:
options: Multiplying the overtime hours by the plain price out of habit

questions.question: The habit that beats the trap is:
options: Writing down the price of that kind of hour — the row — before touching the hours
Rounding all rates to the nearest ten rand

questions.question: One rung of the administrator's ladder equals:
options: One completed year of service, worth R12 000 more per year

questions.question: The ladder R120 000 × R12 000 — R180 000 has how many climbs before the top?
options: Five — sixty thousand of ladder divided by a twelve-thousand rung

questions.question: Paying by ladder makes tomorrow visible because:
options: The worker can read today what year four will pay, and the shop can budget years ahead
Only the owner knows the notches
It hides future pay from the worker

questions.question: The three moves for any salary-scale question are:
options: Add the ceiling, subtract the start, guess the rest
Multiply by twelve, add overtime, subtract tax
Count completed years for the rung; divide the year by twelve; measure the ladder and divide by the rung for the top
